core_obligations: First construction (proof lines 803-808): from a map out of the functor applied to a presheaf the author composes with the unit supplied by the companion result, obtaining a map from the given presheaf; the construction is functorial by inspection.

Second construction (proof lines 811-824): from a map into the other functor the author applies the first functor, then uses a canonical map from the values of the composite on the auxiliary category to the value at the object, gets a map of presheaves by functoriality, and composes to obtain the desired map.

Closing (proof lines 799-800, 821-822): the author leaves to the reader the verification that the two constructions are inverse to each other, and notes that one of the intermediate steps is a trivial verification of functoriality.
proof_roadmap: Construct a map in one direction by composing with the unit.
Construct the map in the other direction by composing with a canonical map out of the composite.
Leave the verification that the constructions are inverse to the reader.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the two functors on presheaves attached to a functor of categories are adjoint, that is, that the displayed bijection of morphism sets holds bifunctorially (statement lines 783-793). The proof is a complete construction of the two maps: one is obtained by composing with the unit supplied by a companion result (proof lines 803-808), the other by applying the first functor and composing with a canonical map from the values of the composite, whose functoriality is noted to be immediate (proof lines 811-824). The non-formal content is the construction of the two maps; the author explicitly leaves to the reader only the verification that they are inverse to each other (proof lines 799-800). The claim is H1/H2: a short construction in both directions with the routine verification noted.
